items.question: What status does the eight-syllabled mantra hold among all mantras?
premises: The eight-syllabled mantra is declared.
It is spoken as the essence of mantras.
items.inference: The eight-syllabled mantra is the essential core among all mantras.
items.plain_english: The eight-syllabled mantra is declared and spoken of as the essence of all mantras.

rows.grounds: compound object indicating number of syllables
compound referring to half of that number

items.question: On which materials should twelve syllables and their half be written?
premises: Twelve syllables are associated with birch bark.
Half of that number is associated with a copper plate.
items.inference: Twelve syllables should be written on birch bark and six on a copper plate.
uncertainties: The verb of writing is implied rather than explicit.
items.plain_english: Write twelve syllables on birch bark and half that number on a copper plate.

rows.grounds: optative or imperative sense in benediction

items.question: For what purpose should these agents consecrate the recipient?
premises: These agents are invoked to consecrate you.
The stated purpose is the accomplishment of dharma, desire, and wealth.
items.inference: The consecration aims at achieving dharma, desire, and wealth.
uncertainties: The identity of 'these' is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: May these consecrate you for the accomplishment of dharma, desire, and wealth.

items.question: What ritual sequence is prescribed across all tantric texts?
premises: Meditation, worship, and recitation are listed in order.
This order is stated to apply in all tantras.
items.inference: The universal tantric sequence is meditation, then worship, then recitation.
items.plain_english: Meditation, worship, and recitation—this is the sequence in all tantras.

items.question: Why must the script be placed at the beginning of the rite?
premises: What is done without this is known to be fruitless.
Therefore the script should be placed at the beginning.
items.inference: Placing the script first is necessary for the rite to bear fruit.
uncertainties: The specific script or syllables are not named here.
items.plain_english: One should know that what is done is fruitless; therefore one should place the script at the beginning.

items.question: What harmful consequence follows from performing abbreviated worship incorrectly?
premises: The condition described is doing otherwise.
Abbreviated worship would become harm-causing.
items.inference: If performed otherwise, abbreviated worship brings harm instead of benefit.
items.plain_english: Otherwise, O Goddess, abbreviated worship would become harmful.

items.question: What concluding injunction is given regarding satisfying the deity?
premises: The verb enjoins causing satisfaction.
The quotative marks this as a concluding instruction.
items.inference: The practitioner should satisfy the deity.
uncertainties: The object to be satisfied is implied from context.
items.plain_english: Thus, one should satisfy.

items.question: How should abbreviated worship be performed within the circle?
premises: The deity is first invoked in the middle of the circle.
Abbreviated worship should then be performed.
items.inference: After invocation in the circle's center, one should perform abbreviated worship.
items.plain_english: Having invoked in the middle of the circle, one should perform abbreviated worship—thus.

items.question: What actions should follow worship before reciting the mantra?
premises: The goddess is worshipped first.
A flower offering is given to her before mantra recitation.
items.inference: After worship and offering flowers to the goddess, one should recite the mantra.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped, having given a flower offering to the goddess, one should recite the mantra—thus.

items.question: What blessings of peace and longevity are sought through repeated practice?
premises: Peace is wished to arise again and again.
A lifespan of a hundred and eight hundred is wished.
items.inference: Repeated practice is associated with repeated peace and long life.
uncertainties: The expression 'aṣṭottaraṃ śatam' may idiomatically mean one hundred and eight years.
items.plain_english: May there be peace again and again; may one live a hundred and eight hundred years.

items.question: From what kinds of afflictions and sins is one freed?
premises: Freedom is stated in the passive.
The sources include impure, difficult, and even most terrible sins.
items.inference: One is freed from impure hardships and even the most terrible sins.
items.plain_english: One is freed from impure difficulties and from even the most terrible sins.

items.question: What power results from worshipping Krishna with corals?
premises: Krishna is worshipped with corals.
The stated result is bringing the three worlds under control.
items.inference: Worshipping Krishna with corals grants control over the three worlds.
items.plain_english: One should worship Krishna with corals and bring the three worlds under control.

items.question: What certain status is attained by worshipping Krishna with rubies?
premises: Krishna is worshipped with rubies.
The worshipper certainly becomes a king.
items.inference: Worshipping Krishna with rubies certainly makes one a king.
items.plain_english: One should worship Krishna with rubies; one certainly becomes a king.

items.question: What quality is gained by worshipping with emerald gems?
premises: Worship is performed with emerald-made gems.
The worshipper becomes possessed of knowledge.
items.inference: Worshipping with emerald gems leads to becoming knowledgeable.
items.plain_english: Worshipping with emerald gems, one becomes possessed of knowledge.

rows.grounds: compound locative indicating time of death

items.question: What final attainment follows reaching the green abode at death?
premises: At the end of the body one attains the green abode.
After that one obtains the state of liberation.
items.inference: Attaining the green abode at death leads to obtaining liberation.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'haritāṃ' is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: At the end of the body, having attained the green abode, one obtains the state of liberation.

items.question: Which offerings are prescribed for Tuesday and Wednesday worship?
premises: Tuesday is associated with red lotuses.
Wednesday is associated with offerings produced from tagara.
items.inference: One should use red lotuses on Tuesday and tagara-derived offerings on Wednesday.
uncertainties: The main verb of worship is implied from surrounding verses.
items.plain_english: On Tuesday with red lotuses, and on Wednesday with those produced from tagara.

items.question: How should an ascetic perform worship on Saturday?
premises: Saturday worship is specified.
The ascetic should worship with shami flowers and devotion.
items.inference: An ascetic should worship devotedly with shami flowers on Saturday.
items.plain_english: On Saturday, the ascetic should worship with devotion using shami flowers.

items.question: Which offerings are assigned to Wednesday and Thursday in this sequence?
premises: Wednesday is associated with yavaka offerings.
Thursday is associated with offerings produced from supa.
items.inference: Yavaka offerings are used on Wednesday and supa-produced offerings on Thursday.
uncertainties: The exact botanical identity of 'yāvaka' and 'sūpa' is uncertain.
items.plain_english: On Wednesday with yavaka flowers, but on Thursday with those produced from supa.

items.question: What libation is prescribed for the month of Vaishakha?
premises: The time specified is the month of Vaishakha.
Libations should be offered according to rule with snow-cold waters.
items.inference: In Vaishakha one should duly offer libations with snow-cold waters.
items.plain_english: In the month of Vaishakha, one should duly offer libations with snow-cold waters.

items.question: How should Hari be worshipped during the month of Ashadha?
premises: The time specified is the month of Ashadha.
Hari should be worshipped according to rule with sacred threads.
items.inference: In Ashadha one should duly worship Hari with sacred threads.
items.plain_english: In the month of Ashadha, one should duly worship Hari with sacred threads.

items.question: To whom should offerings be presented at the end of worship?
premises: The time specified is the end of worship.
Offerings should be presented to the king of gods and to the queens.
items.inference: At the conclusion of worship, offerings go to Indra and his queens.
items.plain_english: At the end of worship, one should offer to the king of the gods and to the queens.

items.question: What reward comes from performing this practice for a full year?
premises: The practitioner performs the practice thus for a year.
The result is obtaining the desired object.
items.inference: A year of this practice yields the desired attainment.
items.plain_english: Thus, having practiced for a year, the practitioner obtains the desired object.

items.question: With what offerings should Krishna be worshipped in Shravana?
premises: The time specified is the month of Shravana.
Krishna should be worshipped with offerings produced from ketaka.
items.inference: In Shravana one should worship Krishna with ketaka-derived offerings.
items.plain_english: In the month of Shravana, one should indeed worship Krishna with offerings produced from ketaka.

items.question: What fruits should be offered abundantly in this ritual context?
premises: Cardamom, clove, and kakkola fruits are specified.
They should be offered in many ways or abundantly.
items.inference: One should abundantly offer cardamom, clove, and kakkola fruits.
uncertainties: The exact identity of 'kakkola' is uncertain.
items.plain_english: One should offer cardamom, clove, and kakkola fruits in abundance.
